subject_rule: Limited to one programme, the two-year Master's in China Studies, in which each scholar picks one of six research areas; applicants may hold a bachelor's degree in any field and need not have studied China before.

notes: 6 research areas recorded; the source names six. There is only one programme (Master's Program in China Studies), taught at Yenching Academy; the research area sets the diploma title, not the course requirements. Scholars may take electives from any of the six areas.

Graduation needs a passed thesis plus at least 31 credits (international students and students from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan) or 34 credits (Mainland Chinese students). Core courses: China in Transition, Chinese Language, Field Study, Topics in China Studies Lecture Series, Academic Writing.
Eligibility on the subject of the applicant's first degree: a bachelor's degree in any field (or enrolled and graduating in August of the enrolment year). No restriction on undergraduate major.

Partner universities (the Academy lists 12 in South America, 3 in Africa and Oceania, 13 in Asia, 19 in Europe and 27 in North America, 74 in all): their students and alumni must apply through their own university's pre-selection, which nominates students for interview. Cooperating universities (9 in Asia, 14 in Europe, 17 in North America, 5 in South America, none in Africa and Oceania, 45 in all) do not pre-select; their students and graduates apply directly on the Academy's online portal. Students from other universities are not stated to be excluded; the only stated requirement is a bachelor's degree in any field.

Partner universities named include: Boğaziçi University, Duke Kunshan University, IDC Herzliya, Kyoto University, Middle East Technical University, NYU Abu Dhabi, NYU Shanghai, Sungkyunkwan University, University of Delhi, University of Hong Kong (Faculty of Arts), Vietnam National University, Waseda University, Yale-NUS College; KU Leuven, Leiden University, Lomonosov Moscow State University, LMU Munich, Sapienza University of Rome, Sciences Po Bordeaux, SOAS University of London, St Petersburg University, Trinity College Cambridge, Trinity College Dublin, Ca' Foscari Venice, University of Milan, University of Naples L'Orientale, University College Dublin, University College London, University of Copenhagen, Durham University, University of Edinburgh, University of Torino; Arizona State University (Barrett Honors College), Columbia, Dartmouth, Georgetown, Harvard, Harvard Kennedy School, Indiana University Bloomington, Northwestern, Rice, Stanford, University of Chicago, UNC Chapel Hill, UNAM, UBC, UC Berkeley, UCLA, UC Santa Barbara, University of Michigan, University of Minnesota Honors Program, Notre Dame, University of Rochester, University of Toronto, University of Virginia, University of Washington, University of Wisconsin-Madison, Washington University in St. Louis, Wellesley College; FGV, Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Chile, Universidad Catolica Argentina, Universidad de San Andres, Universidad del Salvador, Universidad Torcuato Di Tella, University of Brasilia, University of Buenos Aires, University of Campinas, University of Chile (Institute of International Studies, School of Economics and Business, School of Law); University of Auckland, University of Cape Town, University of Melbourne.
The partner-university list is read from the Academy page; the page can change each cycle.
